tasks.short: Design the plate or buffet display, make and photograph a sample, show cooks how to plate, check allergens, put out allergen cards and write plating instructions.

steps.what: Chef determines how food should be presented on the plate or buffet
Chef makes a sample plate and photographs it
Chef shows cooks how to create decorative food displays
Chef checks the dish's ingredients and allergens in the recipe record against the dish as made, and which buffet dish each card goes with
Chef makes the allergen cards and puts them out at the buffet: written by hand today; after the change printed from the checked list and put out
Chef writes plating instructions for the recipe card

tasks.design: The recipe app ({OTHER}) holds each dish's ingredients, allergens, plating photo and steps. Once the chef has checked the allergen list, the app prints the buffet allergen cards from it instead of writing them by hand. Designing the presentation, making samples and showing cooks stay with the chef.
tasks.previous_blocker: Allergen cards and plating notes were written by hand for each event.
tasks.enabler_now: Recipe apps hold allergen data and photos and print cards.
tasks.still_hard: A recipe change that is not entered makes the card wrong.
tasks.human_edge: Making a buffet look generous without waste.

reach.learn: Whether printed cards cut allergen errors.

evidence.claim: Recipe apps hold allergen data, plating photos and steps per dish and print cards.
Guests must get information on the 14 EU allergens; in 2022 only 41% of inspected horeca businesses complied.

assumptions: Boundary: from presentation design to cards and instructions; cooking is outside.
Input contract: recipes and allergens entered by the chef in the recipe app; fallback is handwritten cards.

Designing, making samples, showing cooks and checking allergens keep their full time. Cards keep 20 for printing and putting them out; s6 keeps 90 because the plating photo sits with the recipe and the chef still writes the steps.
Every recipe change is checked by the chef before cards are printed.

incremental.description: Chef keeps recipe allergen data current.

approvals.approved_version: The allergen card text exactly as checked by the chef in s4 against the dish as made, printed once and placed with that dish on the buffet; a changed recipe needs a new check before cards are printed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: daily specials change too often to be in the recipe app, so about half of the cards are still written by hand (4.5); high: most buffet dishes are in the app (7.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Forecast the week's covers, work out prep lists, decide staffing per shift, build the kitchen roster, brief cooks and adjust for late changes.

steps.what: Chef estimates the week's covers from bookings and experience
Chef works out daily prep lists from the forecast and menu today; after the change the recipe app proposes them and the chef checks them against stock on hand
Chef determines staff requirements per shift
Chef builds the kitchen roster
Chef checks the final roster before it goes out: each cook's shifts, hours against the cao and the staffing need
Chef publishes the checked roster to the kitchen staff
Chef briefs cooks on the week's plan
Chef adjusts the plan for late bookings and absences

tasks.design: A forecast in the kitchen planning tool ({OTHER}) proposes covers per day from till history ({OPS_SYSTEM}), bookings and the weather, and the chef adjusts it. The recipe app turns the adjusted forecast into prep lists, and productivity norms suggest cooks per shift for the chef to decide. The roster tool checks the cao's on-call notice, and the chef checks the final roster before publishing it to the cooks. No shift is allocated by ranking individual staff; briefing and late changes stay with the chef.
tasks.previous_blocker: Covers, prep lists and staffing were worked out in spreadsheets from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Sales forecasts from till data exist for restaurants, and recipe apps scale prep lists.
tasks.still_hard: Events in town and the weather upset forecasts; the chef's correction matters.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing that a sunny Sunday means double the terrace orders.
tasks.altitude: The chef adjusts a forecast and suggested staffing instead of building them.

reach.learn: Whether one forecast serves kitchen and floor.

evidence.claim: At Nando's Singapore a sales forecast was 25% more accurate, 30% after manager adjustments, and sales per labour hour rose 15% (vendor case, four-site pilot).
The Horeca cao lets on-call staff be called 24 hours ahead; the law says 4 days.
A headcount forecast is outside Annex III; ranking staff for shifts is high-risk.

assumptions: Boundary: from forecast to adjusted plan; payroll is outside.
Input contract: till history from the POS; bookings from the reservation system; productivity norms set by the chef; fallback is spreadsheets.

Briefing, late changes and the roster check and publication keep their full time. s1 keeps 40 for adjusting the forecast; s2 keeps 15 for checking proposed prep lists; s3 keeps 60 because norms suggest cooks per shift and the chef decides; s4 keeps 70 because cao checks are done by the tool and placing people stays.
Forecasts are about covers, not about individual cooks.

already_counted.description: Chef adjusts the forecast and staffing suggestion.

approvals.approved_version: The kitchen roster for the week exactly as checked by the chef in s4c, published once to the kitchen staff in the roster tool; any change needs a new check and publication.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: in a small kitchen with many walk-ins and events the forecast is often off, so most of it and the prep lists are redone by hand (26.4); high: steady trade where the forecast holds (39.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take event enquiries, meet the customer about the menu, write a priced proposal, send it and adjust after feedback.

steps.what: Customer phones or e-mails the restaurant about an event
Chef takes event enquiries by e-mail and phone
Chef meets with customers to discuss menus for weddings, parties or banquets
Chef writes the menu proposal with prices
Chef checks the final proposal: dishes, allergens against the dietary needs, price per guest and the customer it goes to
Chef sends the checked proposal to the customer: by e-mail today, from the recipe app after the change
Chef adjusts the menu after the customer's feedback

tasks.design: An enquiry form on the restaurant's website ({CMS}) captures date, guest numbers, budget and dietary needs before the chef calls back. A proposal template in the recipe app ({OTHER}) fills chosen dishes with portion costs, allergens and a price per guest; the chef checks the final proposal and its recipient, and only then sends it. Meeting the customer and adjusting the menu stay with the chef.
tasks.previous_blocker: Enquiries came without key details, and proposals were written and costed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Recipe apps hold portion costs and allergens and fill proposal templates.
tasks.still_hard: Customers change their minds; the conversation sets the menu.
tasks.human_edge: Turning a couple's story into a menu they remember.

reach.learn: Whether costed templates speed up quotes.

evidence.claim: Apicbase rolls ingredient prices up to portion cost and applies suppliers' price changes.
Guests must get information on the 14 EU allergens.

assumptions: Boundary: from enquiry to agreed menu; the event itself is outside.
Input contract: enquiries from customers through the form; portion costs from the recipe app; fallback is e-mail and hand costing.

Meeting, adjusting and the final check keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 because the form gives the facts and calling back stays; s3 keeps 50 because dishes, costs and allergens fill in and the chef chooses the menu; sending keeps 25.
Customers' time is outside the chef's savings.

incremental.description: Chef keeps event dishes in the recipe app.
Customers fill in date, guest numbers, budget and dietary needs in the enquiry form (part moved from the chef's questions).

approvals.approved_version: The menu proposal with dishes, allergens and price per guest exactly as checked by the chef in s3c, sent once to the customer who made the enquiry; any change needs a new check before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most customers still phone instead of using the form and many events need dishes not in the app (11.1); high: form and app used as designed (23.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write the job ad, read applications, arrange interviews, interview and hold trial shifts, and decide and make the offer.

steps.what: Chef writes the job ad for cooks and kitchen workers
Chef checks the final job ad: role, hours, pay, requirements and where it will be published
Chef publishes the checked job ad from the applicant tracking system
Chef reads applications and picks candidates to meet
Chef checks who gets a booking link: each candidate on the shortlist, their contact details and whether it is an interview or a trial shift
Chef arranges interviews: by phoning candidates today; after the change by sending the checked candidates a booking link
Chef interviews candidates and holds trial shifts
Chef decides whom to hire and makes the offer

tasks.design: Job ads start from the restaurant's earlier ads in the applicant tracking system ({ATS}), and applications arrive there with a few fixed questions (availability, hygiene certificate), sorted but never rejected automatically; the chef reads every application. The chef checks the final ad before publishing it. Once the chef has picked and checked the candidates, the chef sends them a link to book an interview or trial shift. Interviews and the hiring decision stay with the chef.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applications came by e-mail and interviews were arranged by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Applicant tracking systems hold ads, screening questions and self-booking links.
tasks.still_hard: Good cooks show themselves in a trial shift, not on paper.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing in a trial shift who keeps calm when the tickets pile up.

evidence.claim: Applicant tracking systems hold ads, screening questions and interview booking links.
Decisions based solely on automated processing with significant effect are barred; the chef reads every application.

assumptions: Boundary: from vacancy to offer; contracts and onboarding are outside.
Input contract: applications from candidates through the ATS; fixed questions set by the chef; fallback is e-mail and phone.

Interviews, decisions and both checks keep their full time. s1 keeps 70 because an earlier ad is the start and the chef rewrites it; s2 keeps 70 because the chef reads every application; s3 keeps 10 for sending links and rebooking.
No AI screens or ranks candidates.

incremental.description: Chef sets up interview slots in the ATS.

approvals.approved_version: The booking link for an interview or trial shift, sent once to each candidate on the shortlist as checked by the chef in s3c; other candidates need a new check.
The job ad exactly as checked by the chef in s1c, published once on the job sites named there for this vacancy; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many candidates do not use the booking link and need a call, and earlier ads fit few vacancies (15.3); high: candidates book online (21.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The chef keeps cooking, presentation, customers and hiring decisions; spreadsheets, handwritten cards and phone rounds shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A chef whose planning is ready on Monday morning and who spends the week at the stove.
